description:
We're a crew of four Computer Science students teaming up for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

We write code, build web apps, and train AI. But we also know how to pitch an idea—we're just as passionate about storytelling, communication, and the business side of tech.

Great tech fails if no one understands it. We balance heavy coding with clear narratives. We don't just build working prototypes; we build practical solutions that make sense in the real world.
summary: Moonwalker is a browser-based space mission simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It gives students, space fans, and aspiring engineers a hands-on way to learn how real spaceflight works. Players recreate iconic missions like Apollo 11, Voyager, and JWST by balancing rocket weight, fuel, and cargo limits. Using real rocket math and orbital mechanics, the game tests whether your craft actually makes it to its target.
details: Moonwalker is an interactive web-based space mission design and simulation game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The application empowers students, space enthusiasts, and future engineers to explore the real complexities of space exploration by planning and executing authentic missions (such as Apollo 11, Voyager, Hubble, JWST, and Mars Curiosity). Players manage real engineering trade-offs—such as balancing dry mass, propellant loads, and payload constraints—while applying the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and Keplerian orbital mechanics to ensure successful trajectory execution and mission outcomes.
